# Security

NHS England takes security and the protection of private data extremely
seriously. If you believe you have found a vulnerability or other issue that
could compromise a system or private data, please report it privately using one
of the routes below.

This policy is a starting point for repositories created from this template.
Before using it for a specific NHS project, maintainers must confirm the scope,
supported versions, and reporting routes.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please report suspected vulnerabilities privately. Do not create a public issue
or pull request containing vulnerability details. If you are unsure whether an
issue is security-related, use a private reporting route.

### Email

Email is the preferred reporting method. Include as much of the following
information as you can safely provide:

- The affected project, service, component, and version.
- A description of the potential security impact.
- Steps to reproduce the issue and any relevant evidence.
- A way to contact you for follow-up.

Do not include patient-identifiable information, credentials, secrets, or other
sensitive data in an email or public issue. Use an approved secure method if
sensitive evidence is required.

Send reports to [cybersecurity@nhs.net](mailto:cybersecurity@nhs.net).

Before adopting this template, confirm that this mailbox is the correct route
for the project. If it is not, replace it with a monitored, approved private
reporting contact.

### National Cyber Security Centre

The
[NCSC vulnerability reporting guidance](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/information/vulnerability-reporting)
directs reports about UK government online services to the
[Government Vulnerability Reporting Service](https://vulnerability-reporting.service.security.gov.uk/).
Check that this service is appropriate for your report. It is not a substitute
for confirming the correct reporting route for a particular NHS project.

## Disclosure process

The organisation receiving a report will assess it and determine the appropriate
next steps. Coordinate any public disclosure with the team handling the report.
Do not publish vulnerability details before that discussion.
